statement: A complex number is a number of the form z = x + iy (or a + bi), where x and y are real numbers and i is the imaginary unit.

properties.property: Triangle inequality: |z_1 + z_2| <= |z_1| + |z_2| for any complex numbers z_1 and z_2
properties.why: Follows directly from the definition of the complex modulus

properties.property: Euler's formula: exp(i*phi) = cos(phi) + i*sin(phi) for any real phi, with Euler's identity exp(i*pi) = -1
properties.why: Follows from convergent power series expansions of exp, cos, and sin

properties.property: Complex logarithm: log w = ln|w| + i*arg(w) for any non-zero complex number w
properties.why: Inverts exp(z) = w, inheriting multivaluedness from arg(w) due to exp(z + 2*pi*i) = exp(z)

properties.property: Complex exponentiation: z^omega = exp(omega * ln(z)), which is multivalued unless omega is an integer
properties.why: Defined via the multivalued complex logarithm

properties.property: Algebraic closure: any non-empty complex square matrix has at least one complex eigenvalue, and any nonconstant polynomial has a root in C
properties.why: Fundamental algebraic property of the field of complex numbers

properties.property: Cauchy-Riemann equations: a real-differentiable function f: C -> C is complex differentiable (holomorphic) if and only if df/d(z_bar) = 0
properties.why: Imposed by the condition that the difference quotient limit exists independent of approaching direction

assumptions.assumption: For the complex logarithm log w, the argument must be non-zero (w in C^x)
assumptions.breaks_when: w = 0, where the complex logarithm is undefined

assumptions.assumption: For the principal value of the complex logarithm ln z, the domain is restricted to C \ (-R_>=0)
assumptions.breaks_when: z is a non-positive real number (along the negative real axis branch cut), where continuity fails

assumptions.assumption: For trigonometric/hyperbolic quotient functions (e.g., tan z, cot z), denominators must be non-zero
assumptions.breaks_when: Expressions evaluate to infinity or involve division by zero

failure_modes.mode: Failure of power and logarithm identities
failure_modes.signature: a^(bc) != (a^b)^c or ambiguous multiple values under evaluation
failure_modes.cause: Complex exponentiation is multivalued when exponents are non-integers; treating multi-valued functions naively as single-valued yields left-hand values that are merely a subset of right-hand values

failure_modes.signature: Logarithm yields infinitely many solutions differing by integer multiples of 2*pi*i (e.g., exp(i*pi) = exp(3*i*pi) = -1)
failure_modes.cause: Periodicity of the complex exponential exp(z + 2*pi*i) = exp(z)

failure_modes.signature: Jump discontinuity in imaginary part across the negative real axis
failure_modes.cause: Restricting the imaginary part of the logarithm to (-pi, pi] to select a principal value
